note: Authored ground truth for CORPUS.md §2.14(a). Five documents, five roles. The unit list is what a correct extractor should find, written before the extractor existed.

units.text: A batch must be acknowledged within two seconds.
A batch is committed whole or not at all; partial ingestion never occurs.
Rejected batches remain retrievable for thirty days.
Operators can replay any accepted batch without engineering involvement.
Ingestion is queue-backed; batches are acknowledged before processing.
units.rationale: Synchronous validation cannot meet the acknowledgement budget under load.

units.text: Schemas are declared by the customer, never inferred.
units.rationale: Inference was the dominant incident source in the previous system.

units.text: Modules are named for what they do, not for the pattern they use.
Never swallow an error to keep a request alive.
Every bug fix ships with the test that would have caught it.
A new runtime dependency requires a written reason in the pull request.
Do not delete queued batches; they are the only copy until the warehouse commit succeeds.

nearDuplicates.why: The same latency constraint stated in a PRD and in an ADR. Almost no shared content words, so a lexical threshold cannot merge them and an embedding must. Measured Jaccard is asserted by the --check run below.

a.text: No user should ever wait more than two seconds for a batch to be acknowledged.

b.text: The p95 acknowledgement budget for a single submission is 2000 milliseconds.

nearDuplicates.why: Whole-batch atomicity, stated as a requirement and as a decision rationale.

a.text: A batch that fails validation must be rejected whole. Partial ingestion is never acceptable.

b.text: A submission is committed in one transaction or not at all.
